chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nahdī, from Yaḥyā ibn Yasār al-Qanbarī, who said:
Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام bequeathed to his son al-Ḥasan before his passing by four months, and he made me a witness to that, along with a group of the mawālī.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam making the designation
key_terms.أَوْصَى: he bequeathed or designated by testament
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ: al-Ḥasan, the son designated in the report
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: the affiliates or close followers present as witnesses

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the designation of Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report records that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام explicitly designated his son al-Ḥasan عليه السلام before his passing and had witnesses present for it. Its significance lies in documenting a witnessed transfer of authority within the line of the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Yahya Bin Yasaar Al Qanbary who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (10th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) bequeathed to his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) before his<sup>asws</sup> passing away by four months and kept me as a witness upon that, and a group of friends’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Yahya ibn Yasar al-Qanbar who has said the following.

“Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) prepared his directive will to his son, al-Hassan four months before his leaving this world. He appointed me to bear testimony to his will as well as a group of the follower friends.”
